S1 BLOCKING — Sculpt Spells still drops the printed exclusion of the caster from its target set.
Invariant and authority: owning bead O4 requires repair or source-backed disposition of truncated qualifiers in non-creature projected targets; registry targeting-qualifiers (opus:F-35) says targeting qualifiers are complete. ADR 0020 preserves source fidelity, including partial structured projections, without requiring deterministic execution of the whole feature.
Locations: packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts:5605 (targets: chosen-creatures); packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json:84124; packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts:3758; visibility-only evidence at packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/alternativeOptionProjections.test.ts:453.
Concrete scenario: an evoker stands inside their own fireball's area and can see themself. The SRD p.54 permits choosing a number of the OTHER creatures affected by the evocation spell. The emitted autoSucceedSave effect contains only chosen-creatures, requiresSight:true, countFormula and noDamageInsteadOfHalf. It carries neither the other-than-caster restriction nor a linked target eligibility predicate. Selecting the visible caster therefore meets every represented target restriction although the printed source excludes them. This is a source-projection defect, not a claim that a current deterministic capability executes Sculpt Spells. Retaining accurate prose mitigates adjudication risk but does not satisfy the explicit O4 projection-repair obligation.
Sibling/state analysis: independently enumerated 84 target-like fields over 73 non-creature records (target/targets/targetTypes/targetQualifier/excludesTargetTypes), including linked mechanics and activation payloads. Searched their source text for other/another/excluding/self, sight, range, type, size and eligibility qualifiers. The other-than-user sibling on Javelin of Lightning preserves excludes:[user,attack-target]; fighter Protection's separate bounded target contract preserves mustBeOtherThanYou. Sculpt Spells is the only chosen-creatures/autoSucceedSave producer. Varied caster versus other visible affected creature while holding visibility, spell and count constant; also examined unseen others. No further visibility omission found. Requirements may legitimately survive in linked fields rather than in the target string itself.
Closure condition: preserve the printed eligible target set through the compiler input and validated projection (other creatures affected by the evocation spell, including explicit self-exclusion or equally clear target wording), regenerate, and add source-backed evidence that distinguishes the visible caster from a visible eligible other creature. A focused exact source regression is proportionate here: one real producer and one independently printed self-exclusion; retain the existing generalized visibility evidence and do not require a universal targeting engine. Reconcile the registry/PR targeting disposition and refresh the PR's stale pre-repair generated-record count/summary to the final scope. Owner: 19.3.1. Repair is MATERIAL (source-semantic target contract); requires fresh full review at the successor head.

S2 BLOCKING — New spell-only option mechanics violate the character resolver's declared option contract.
Invariant and authority: the accepted O5 extension must remain coherent across schema, producer and actual consumer boundary; existing runtime contracts remain operative under design-and-pr-review-policy.md, and AGENTS.md's public-surface convention governs the exposed RulesPackCharacterResolver. Its returned FeatureChoice.options use FeatureChoiceOption, which currently promises that every present mechanics object contains a nonoptional proficiency effects array.
Locations: packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts:579 newly admits spellGrants without effects; packages/core/src/rules/featureChoices.ts:111-112 still declares mechanics?: {effects: readonly ProficiencyGrantEffect[]}; packages/core/src/character/rulesPackResolver.ts:1231 casts generated choices to FeatureChoice[]; emitted Pact of the Chain mechanics at packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json:85805.
Concrete scenario: called the real getBundledDnd5eCharacterResolver().listFeatures(), found feature:warlock:pact-boon's Pact of the Chain option, and observed mechanics={spellGrants:[{spell:spell:find-familiar}]} with effects===undefined. A caller using the declared contract after checking mechanics and invoking mechanics.effects.map(e=>e.kind) throws TypeError on this real bundled record. The same contract also hides spellGrants from typed consumers. This is an actual producer/type mismatch; it does not require inventing a new deterministic spell-grant consumer.
Sibling/state analysis: enumerated every returned feature option with mechanics through the real resolver. Exactly two exist: Beguiling Influence (valid proficiency effects array) and Pact of the Chain (the sole violation). Options without mechanics remain valid. The current proficiency consumer defensively checks Array.isArray(mechanics.effects) and safely ignores spell-only mechanics, so no existing creation crash is claimed; that limits consequence but does not remove the published return-contract defect. Reviewed the schema's effects-only, spell-only and combined shapes and the shared FeatureChoice type path.
Closure condition: align the shared option-mechanics type and documentation with the validated effects/spellGrants shapes, keeping proficiency behavior and the option-local grant. Ensure the real resolver returns objects conforming to that type; review callers for the resulting optional/union narrowing. Permanent evidence should be proportionate: existing real Pact/Beguiling assertions plus typecheck and, if needed, one small producer/schema/type boundary check; no new proof framework or spell execution is required. Owner: 19.3.1. Repair is MATERIAL (shared runtime return-contract change), even if implemented only as type alignment.
